title: French Toast
subtitle: Pain perdu with cinnamon and honey
excerpt: French toast is made by soaking thick slices of bread in a spiced egg and milk mixture, then frying in butter until golden. It works with any white bread that is one or two days old. Serve with a drizzle of honey.
sourceNotes: Pain perdu, meaning lost bread, has roots in medieval France as a way to use stale bread. The British and American version is nearly identical.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The egg mixture can be made the night before and kept covered in the fridge.

content.text: Use bread that is at least one day old. Fresh bread soaks up too much egg mixture and turns soft in the middle. You want 4 to 6 thick slices of white bread, about 2 cm thick.
Whisk together the eggs, milk, and cinnamon in a wide shallow bowl. Add a small pinch of salt.
Dip 2 slices of bread into the mixture. Let them soak for 20 seconds per side.
Melt a knob of butter in the pan over a medium heat.
Add the soaked bread. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes on each side until deep golden.
Remove and keep warm. Repeat with the remaining slices.
Serve with a drizzle of honey.

items.symptom: The toast is golden outside but soggy in the middle.
items.cause: The bread soaked too long or was too fresh.
items.fix: Use day-old bread and soak for 20 seconds only per side.

items.symptom: The butter is burning before the toast is cooked.
items.cause: The pan heat is too high.
items.fix: Lower the heat to medium-low and add a little more butter.

items.symptom: The egg mixture runs off the bread without soaking in.
items.cause: The bread is too dry or was not submerged.
items.fix: Press bread gently into the bowl to help absorption.
